title: UNESCO verifies damage to 501 cultural sites in Ukraine since February 2022
body:
As of 25 June 2025, UNESCO had verified damage to 501 cultural sites in Ukraine since 24 February 2022, according to its Ukraine war page. The breakdown was 262 buildings of historical or artistic interest, 151 religious sites, 34 museums, 33 monuments, 18 libraries, two archaeological sites and one archive.

UNESCO describes these as preliminary figures produced by cross-checking reported incidents, and says they do not commit the organisation. The same page recorded the deaths of 22 journalists and media workers, and 4,163 educational institutions destroyed or damaged, of which 3,798 were damaged and 365 destroyed, according to Ukraine's Ministry of Education and Science.

UNESCO's verified count has risen over time. It had verified damage to 260 sites by 19 June 2023, and it listed 515 sites as of 7 January 2026, including 153 religious sites, 268 buildings of historical or artistic interest and 38 museums, according to later versions of its list. The World Heritage Committee has also placed Saint Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv and the historic centre of Lviv on the List of World Heritage in Danger, noting that they remained under permanent threat since the start of the invasion.
